header.stance: 前端殖利率回升，風險偏好仍穩

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## Fed重申穩定物價，短債回吐前一日漲勢

油價續跌、美股上漲，美債週五卻走弱。2年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.21%，完全回吐週四漲幅；10年期上升2個基點至4.56%。Fed半年度報告一方面肯定經濟與生產力成長，另一方面強調通膨仍遠高於目標，讓投資人難以只憑原油下跌，就期待政策壓力減輕。

賣壓集中在前端。10年期實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率各上升1個基點，分別至2.32%及2.24%；30年期名目殖利率微升至5.06%，實質殖利率則未變。長期借款成本仍高，但這次並非由長端領跌。

日本走勢相反。政府呼籲退休基金增加本地投資，帶動日債大漲、日圓升值，雖然配置規範尚未改變。信用市場則面對偏緊的估值：公司債利差接近數十年低點，交易商持有淨空頭，融資活動雖仍正常，價格緩衝卻有限。需要新資金、債權保障或高成本再融資的企業，與整體市場的良好氣氛仍有落差。

## 前端再次承壓，市場等待通膨驗證Fed立場

2年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.21%，5年期上升3個基點至4.30%，10年期上升2個基點至4.56%，30年期上升1個基點至5.06%。2年與10年期利差收窄3個基點至35，2年與30年期利差收窄4個基點至85，反轉前一天的牛市趨陡。市場對預期升息期間的調整最明顯。

實質利率的壓力同樣偏向中短端。5年期上升3個基點至2.02%，7年期上升2個基點至2.16%，10年期上升1個基點至2.32%，20年與30年期維持2.66%及2.86%。10年期名目殖利率的2個基點升幅，由實質利率與通膨補償各貢獻一半，後者收在2.24%。

若拉長至一個月，實質利率仍是主要變化：10年期實質殖利率上升12個基點，損益兩平通膨率下降9個基點。本週2、5及10年期名目殖利率各上升7個基點，30年期上升8個基點。週四的反彈，並未明顯改變整週的融資環境。

Fed《貨幣政策報告》形容經濟成長穩健、生產力強勁、銀行體系有韌性。伊朗戰爭、關稅與科技產品成本使通膨升高，但排除極端項目的截尾通膨指標已放緩。決策者重申穩定物價的承諾，若長期預期受到威脅，將準備強力回應。

前瞻指引不再明確指定政策路徑，使接下來的通膨資料更重要。貨幣市場反映今年至少升息25個基點，外匯選擇權也開始為美國CPI公布前後的事件風險定價。經濟活動強勁，讓Fed有空間維持限制性政策；核心通膨是否真的降溫，比原油再跌一天更有意義。

燃料與食品供應仍是變數。煉油受限、柴油供應中斷，使成品油未能完全跟隨原油下跌。美國農業部7月供需表將美國小麥產量下調至15.36億英斗，並減少玉米及全球穀物庫存估計。不過，這些風險尚未帶動10年期通膨補償大幅上升。

國庫券對較緊政策路徑的反應，主要落在最短天期之外。4週期維持3.69%，6週與8週各上升1個基點至3.69%及3.72%；13週與17週各上升2個基點至3.80%及3.88%；6個月與一年期各上升4個基點至3.96%及4.06%。越往後的升幅越大，較符合預期利率改變，而非眼前現金短缺。

## 公司債利差偏緊，交易商庫存也偏低

本週多數時間，美國公司債對公債的殖利率差約74個基點，接近數十年低點。截至6月，主要交易商今年平均持有約$40億公司債淨空頭，為1998年有資料以來首見。其中，剩餘期限至少5年的債券淨空頭約$137億，部分由較短天期約$96.6億的淨多頭抵銷。

庫存偏低不只有一個原因。高利率與地緣不確定性，降低交易商以窄利差承擔長債的意願；退休基金與保險公司需求強，也可能讓可留在帳上的券不多。此外，電子交易已占投資級49%、高收益32%，交易商能以較少資產負債表部位撮合資金流。平時交易效率提高，卻不代表突然大跌時，交易商一定願意吸收更多風險。

歐洲投資級利差也接近金融危機以來最窄，先前伊朗戰爭帶來的擴大幅度已收復。RBC Wealth Management認為歐元債尤其昂貴，美元與英鎊市場相對較有價值，同時仍肯定企業資產負債表健康。問題在於投資人為這份品質支付的價格。

美債殖利率升高之際，LQD下跌0.23%至$107.46；HYG下跌0.05%至$79.71，JNK下跌0.07%至$95.93。高收益跌幅有限，與股票上漲並存，投資級的價格壓力則較大。

### 消費貸款與可轉債提供不同選擇

Lendable的£5億個人貸款證券化，提供天期較短、逐步攤還本金的曝險。平台累計承作逾£100億消費信貸，2025年營收年增90%至£4.46億，營業利益£1.14億。交易為英國、美國與墨西哥放款拓展資金，同時把無擔保家庭信貸風險移轉給ABS投資人。定期償還本金有別於長天期公司債，但資產表現仍取決於借款人的就業與再融資能力。

MiniMax則搭配增資與可轉債籌資。公司擬以每股HK$268、折價9.9%，發行3,560萬股，募集HK$95億；另發行HK$65億、2027年到期零息可轉債，轉換溢價25%。合計融資接近$20億，支應AI開發。股權與未來轉換可以降低現金利息需求，卻也造成稀釋，股價週五盤中最多下跌9.8%。

銀行放款持續成長，但對企業提供的新動能減弱。6月銀行信貸以年率計增加4.7%，貸款與租賃增加5.2%；工商貸款僅增加3.7%，低於5月10.9%及4月15.9%。存款成長5.3%，其中其他存款增加7.6%，大額定存減少10%。

美東16:15公布的H.8另顯示，截至7月1日的一週，銀行信貸餘額為$19.6151兆，工商貸款$2.8781兆，存款$19.4345兆，均略低於前一週。月度仍成長、週度略轉弱，說明借貸管道正常運作但動能放慢；這份晚盤公布的資料，並非稍早美債賣壓的解釋。

Fed金融穩定評估也呈現整體健康、局部風險集中的情況。家庭與企業債務占GDP比率降至2000年代初以來最低，銀行資本維持高檔，未受存款保險保障的存款較2023年初減少。對沖基金槓桿卻仍接近歷史高點，集中在少數機構。部分私募信貸工具的贖回申請增加，通常在淨資產價值5%的上限內滿足，市場仍正常運作。

### 新資金附帶債權保障，高收益再融資仍昂貴

Aston Martin債權人小組的進一步資料顯示，Arini Capital Management、BlackRock與Sculptor領頭，合計持有逾半數優先擔保票據。他們願意提供新融資，同時要求防止會使既有債權順位下降的交易。公司第一季稅前虧損£6,550萬、淨負債£14.6億，另有等值$18.5億債券於2029年到期。協商焦點已同時涵蓋新增流動性與原有債權保障。

Shapoorji Pallonji的INR2,550億、約$27億再融資中，一筆$6.5億、3年期美元債以14.5%定價。約INR1,500億本幣債面向Farallon、Davidson Kempner及Cerberus等投資人，Deutsche Bank可能投入約$4億。Goswami Infratech債務兩度展延後，新公布的美元條件顯示取得流動性的代價；集團持有18.4%的Tata Sons股權遲遲未能變現，也持續妨礙去槓桿。

紐約收盤後，Central Falls Detention Facility Corp.聲請Chapter 11破產保護。收容率加上每名聯邦拘留者每天約$180的支付，無法支應逾$1.67億債務，這家羅德島營運商希望減免逾$1億負擔。案件為下一交易日增加一項地方政府專案信用風險，顯示免稅債券對設施使用率與集中政府合約的依賴。

## 日本退休基金政策訊號帶動日債，實際配置尚未改變

財務大臣片山皋月呼籲包括GPIF在內的退休基金，增加日本金融資產投資。20年期日債殖利率下降12個基點至3.745%，10年期下降11.5個基點至2.76%，日圓盤中最多升值0.7%。本地買方可能擴大的預期，已足以反轉本週部分壓力。

GPIF管理¥293.6兆資產，約半數配置海外，日本整體另持有約$1.2兆美債。若資金持續移向本地資產，可支持日債、減少結構性的日圓賣壓，卻也可能使海外債券可分配到的資金變少。因此，眼前日債反彈，與長期美債需求受到的影響，方向不一定相同。

目前並無配置規範變更。GPIF由厚生勞動省監督，以五年為策略配置週期，2025年3月檢討時仍維持本地債券、本地股票、海外債券與海外股票各25%。片山的言論先改變了預期，尚未進入投資組合執行。

生產者物價則繼續支持日本央行正常化。6月企業物價指數年增7.1%，為2023年初以來最快，月增0.4%，前月數字也上修；薪資協商結果已連續第三年超過5%。退休基金買盤可穩定債市，卻不會消除企業價格與工資的壓力。

德國CPI終值呈現兩面。6月年增率由5月2.6%降至2.3%，月減0.3%；調和CPI年增2.4%、月減0.2%。能源月減3.0%，主要來自車用燃料與取暖油，但核心通膨維持2.5%，服務價格仍增3.1%。能源降價壓低整體指標，ECB的核心通膨問題卻未解決。

加拿大繼5月增加8.8萬個工作後，6月再增加1.8萬個，就業率升至60.8%，失業率降至6.5%，時薪年增率由3.0%加快至3.3%。製造業減少1.7萬個工作，顯示並非所有部門都強，但較快薪資與較低失業率，仍限制了短期政策轉鬆的理由。

ECB委員Emmanuel Moulin認為，AI資本支出可能在近期推升通膨，之後再透過生產力降低物價壓力，目前尚未因此改變政策。這與Fed面對的難題相近：投資現在支撐活動，效率提升的好處卻要更晚才能實現。

## 巴西通膨低於預期，塞內加爾卻面對融資緊縮

巴西6月通膨年增率降至4.64%，低於調查中所有預測，中位數原為4.80%。月增率降至0.16%，為10月以來最低，食品與飲料下跌0.24%，抵銷住宅成本上漲0.63%的部分影響。5月就業創造偏弱之後，通膨再度帶來利多，提高了連續三次降息後，8月5日再降25個基點的可能。

Selic利率仍為14.25%，央行預測的2026年底通膨也仍高於目標區間上限。大選接近之際，家庭債務重議支持、補貼信貸及暫停部分燃油稅，都增加刺激。眼前物價較溫和，提供漸進降息空間，但財政環境限制了本地殖利率能下行多遠。

塞內加爾的進一步資料，則凸顯既有債務問題的規模。審計發現約$70億未揭露貸款，後續檢討使公共債務估計由GDP的74%提高至130%以上。IMF暫停$18億計畫，信評降至更深的垃圾級，主權已難以使用國際債券市場，外債平均對美債利差超過15個百分點。

今年償債約需CFA5.5兆，預期稅收卻僅約CFA5.4兆。政府愈依賴西非區域市場，銀行持有短期政府券的曝險也愈高。以歐元、美元借款的專案仰賴本幣收入，因此除了債務總額，還款資金能否及時到位也至關重要。重建可信帳目、恢復官方融資，比全球市場單日的利好更有影響。

Absa的區域風險則反映在銀行獲利。淨利息收入占集團營收64%，使肯亞與迦納大幅降息對盈利格外重要。核心監理資本僅略高於董事會11%至12.5%的目標區間，分析師因而質疑收購能力，以及達成16%股東權益報酬率的路徑。投資評等下調後，股價今年約跌10%，南非銀行整體卻漲約7%。問題是收入減弱與擴張餘裕縮小，而非已觸犯資本要求。

即使美債殖利率上升，EMB仍上漲0.03%至$95.99；美元指數僅上升0.03%至100.97，未對借款人增加明顯匯率壓力。指數穩定之下，巴西物價緩解、塞內加爾債務困境及Absa對區域降息的曝險，仍是截然不同的故事。

## 股市與殖利率同升，原油及黃金下跌

S&P 500上漲0.42%至7,575.39，Nasdaq 100上漲0.33%至29,825.11，半導體上漲0.06%至12,967.16，VIX下降5.11%至15.03。投資人接受較高的美債殖利率，並未普遍撤離成長敏感資產。

WTI下跌0.93%至$71.41，布蘭特下跌0.38%至$76.01，仍分別較一週前高3.96%及5.86%，一個月則保持大幅下跌。原油降低了直接通膨壓力，但偏高煉油利潤與地緣干擾，讓燃料成本仍不確定。

實質殖利率升高，黃金下跌0.64%至$4,104.10。美元指數幾乎持平於100.97，因此匯率對金價增加的壓力有限。黃金更像是受到較高實質利率拖累，而非市場全面轉向現金。

平穩匯率與寬廣利差，使G10套利策略今年報酬約8%。不過，美國下一次通膨資料公布前後的避險成本開始上升。Fed指引減少之後，數據若大幅偏離預期，可能擾動有槓桿的利差交易，再經由匯率、新興市場融資與跨境債券需求傳導，即使眼前收盤仍平靜。

## CPI、Warsh聽證與日本配置程序成為焦點

6月CPI與實質所得將於7月14日美東08:30公布，Kevin Warsh於10:00赴眾議院作證；7月15日08:30公布PPI，10:00接著是參議院聽證。核心與服務價格，將檢驗能源降價是否擴散為可持續的通膨降溫，實質所得則呈現購買力變化。Fed週五同時強調成長韌性與穩定物價，Warsh如何解讀新資料因而更重要。

財政部將於7月13日美東11:30發行$920億13週期與$790億26週期國庫券，7月14日同時間再發行$950億42天期，均於7月16日交割。較長國庫券殖利率升幅大於最短天期後，投標與次級交易將顯示貨幣市場資金承接供給是否順暢。

GPIF或厚生勞動省何時正式回應，目前沒有固定日期。啟動配置檢討、修訂目標區間，或對其他公共退休基金提出指引，才是實質進展。沒有這些步驟，週五日債與日圓漲勢能否持續仍不明朗。若真的調整配置，也須連同日本龐大的海外持有部位評估，不能假設支持本地債券就同樣有利美債。

overall_summary.headline: 油價跌、股市漲，Fed限制性立場仍推升短債殖利率
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Fed肯定經濟成長，同時重申穩定物價的承諾，美債由前端領跌。2年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.21%，10年期上升2個基點至4.56%。原油下降，但燃料供應限制及即將公布的通膨資料，讓政策風險仍是焦點。

公司債利差約74個基點，價格緩衝有限，交易商淨空頭集中在長天期。消費貸款證券化、MiniMax增資與可轉債，以及銀行放款仍提供資金；Aston Martin債權人要求新融資搭配保障，Shapoorji Pallonji則以14.5%發行3年期美元債。

日本呼籲退休基金增加本地投資，使20年期日債殖利率下降12個基點，但GPIF配置規範尚未改變。巴西通膨低於預期，塞內加爾償債規模卻接近全年稅收。接下來是CPI、Warsh國會聽證，以及日本是否正式啟動配置調整。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Short Treasuries Give Back Their Rally as the Fed Stresses Price Stability

Treasuries fell Friday even as oil eased and equities rose. The two-year yield increased 5 basis points to 4.21%, reversing Thursday's gain, while the 10-year added 2 to 4.56%. The Fed's semiannual report described solid growth and strong productivity alongside inflation still well above target, leaving investors little reason to regard lower crude as sufficient relief from policy restraint.

The selloff was concentrated toward the front end. Ten-year real yield rose 1 basis point to 2.32%, and breakeven inflation added 1 to 2.24%; the 30-year nominal yield edged up to 5.06% while its real yield stayed unchanged. Long-term borrowing remained costly without another long-end-led selloff.

Japan moved in the opposite direction. A call for pension funds to invest more domestically sent JGB yields sharply lower and strengthened the yen, although no allocation mandate had changed. In credit, spreads near multidecade tights and dealers' net-short corporate holdings left little valuation cushion despite healthy financing activity. Investors continued to distinguish that market-wide backdrop from issuers needing new cash, stronger creditor protections or expensive refinancing.

## Fed Communication Puts the Front End Back Under Pressure

Two-year yields rose 5 basis points to 4.21%, five years added 3 to 4.30%, 10 years gained 2 to 4.56% and 30 years edged up 1 to 5.06%. The move compressed 2s10s by 3 basis points to 35 and 2s30s by 4 to 85. It erased the previous day's bull steepening, with the greatest adjustment around the expected Fed tightening horizon.

Five-year real yield increased 3 basis points to 2.02%, seven years rose 2 to 2.16% and 10 years added 1 to 2.32%. Twenty- and 30-year real yields held at 2.66% and 2.86%. At the 10-year benchmark, the 2-basis-point nominal increase was split equally between real yield and breakeven inflation, which reached 2.24%.

The monthly comparison remained much more heavily weighted toward real rates: 10-year real yield was up 12 basis points and breakeven inflation down 9. Over the week, two-, five- and 10-year nominal yields each rose 7 basis points, while 30 years added 8. Thursday's recovery had done little to change the week's financing conditions.

The Fed's Monetary Policy Report described solid growth, strong productivity and a resilient banking system. Inflation had risen under the effects of the Iran war, tariffs and technology-goods costs, although trimmed measures had eased. Policymakers reiterated their commitment to price stability and readiness to respond forcefully if longer-run expectations were threatened.

Less prescriptive forward guidance put additional weight on the coming inflation releases. Money markets priced at least one 25-basis-point increase this year, while currency options began to assign more event risk around US CPI. Strong activity gave the Fed scope to retain restraint; whether underlying inflation was cooling would matter more than another isolated decline in oil.

Fuel and food costs complicated the disinflation outlook. Refining constraints and disrupted diesel supply had kept refined products from following crude fully lower. USDA's July balance sheet cut US wheat production to 1.536 billion bushels and reduced corn and global grain stocks. Those risks coexisted with only a small increase in 10-year inflation compensation.

Bills followed the firmer policy pricing most clearly beyond the shortest maturities. Four weeks held at 3.69%, six and eight weeks rose 1 basis point to 3.69% and 3.72%, and 13 and 17 weeks added 2 to 3.80% and 3.88%. Six months and one year each rose 4 basis points to 3.96% and 4.06%. The larger increases farther out were consistent with a change in expected rates rather than an immediate shortage of cash.

## Tight Credit Spreads Meet Lean Dealer Books

US corporate bonds had yielded roughly 74 basis points more than Treasuries for much of the week, near multidecade tights. Primary dealers were net short about $4 billion of corporate bonds on average through June, the first such position in data going back to 1998. A roughly $13.7 billion short in maturities of at least five years was partly offset by $9.66 billion of shorter bonds held long.

The figures did not have a single explanation. Higher rates and geopolitical uncertainty discouraged warehousing long bonds at narrow spreads, while pension and insurance demand could leave little inventory available. Electronic execution, now 49% of investment-grade and 32% of high-yield trading, also allowed dealers to match flows with less balance-sheet capacity. Efficient trading in normal conditions nevertheless offered limited evidence of how much risk dealers would absorb during an abrupt selloff.

European investment-grade spreads were also near their tightest since the global financial crisis, having reversed the widening around the Iran war. RBC Wealth Management regarded euro debt as especially expensive and preferred relative value in dollar and sterling markets, while acknowledging healthy corporate balance sheets. The concern was the price paid for that quality.

LQD fell 0.23% to $107.46, while HYG declined 0.05% to $79.71 and JNK 0.07% to $95.93. High yield's limited losses accompanied stronger equities; the larger high-grade decline came as Treasury yields increased.

### Consumer Assets and Convertibles Supply Alternatives

Lendable's £500 million personal-loan securitization offered a shorter, amortizing exposure. The platform had originated more than £10 billion of consumer credit and reported 2025 revenue of £446 million, up 90%, with £114 million of operating profit. The transaction broadened funding for lending in the UK, US and Mexico, while transferring unsecured household-credit risk to ABS investors. Regular principal repayment distinguished the assets from long corporate bonds, but performance still depended on borrowers' employment and ability to refinance.

MiniMax sought HK$9.5 billion through 35.6 million new shares at HK$268, a 9.9% discount, alongside HK$6.5 billion of zero-coupon convertibles due 2027 with a 25% conversion premium. The combined financing approached $2 billion for the AI developer. Equity and future conversion reduced cash-interest needs, at the cost of dilution; shares fell as much as 9.8% Friday.

Bank lending continued to grow, but the business-credit impulse slowed. June bank credit increased at a 4.7% annualized rate and loans and leases at 5.2%. C&I lending grew 3.7%, compared with 10.9% in May and 15.9% in April. Deposits expanded 5.3%, comprising 7.6% growth in other deposits and a 10% contraction in large time deposits.

The H.8 release arrived at 16:15 ET. For the week through July 1, bank credit was $19.6151 trillion, C&I loans $2.8781 trillion and deposits $19.4345 trillion, each slightly below the preceding week. Monthly expansion and weekly softness pointed to an operating lending channel with less momentum, rather than explaining the earlier Treasury selloff.

The Fed's stability assessment likewise separated healthy aggregate balance sheets from concentrated risks. Household and business debt relative to GDP was the lowest since the early 2000s, bank capital remained high and uninsured deposits had declined since early 2023. Hedge-fund leverage remained near record highs, concentrated in a small group. Some private-credit vehicles faced more redemption requests, generally meeting them up to 5% of net asset value while markets continued to function normally.

### New Cash Comes With Creditor Protections and High Coupons

Further detail on Aston Martin's creditor group identified Arini Capital Management, BlackRock and Sculptor as leaders. Holders of more than half the senior secured notes offered fresh financing while seeking to prevent transactions that could subordinate existing claims. The company's £65.5 million first-quarter pretax loss and £1.46 billion net debt sat against $1.85 billion equivalent of bonds due in 2029. The negotiations now centered on both new liquidity and the protections attached to existing debt.

Shapoorji Pallonji's INR255 billion, or $2.7 billion, refinancing included a $650 million three-year dollar bond priced at 14.5%. Roughly INR150 billion of local bonds were directed to investors including Farallon, Davidson Kempner and Cerberus, while Deutsche Bank could invest about $400 million. The additional dollar terms showed the cost of securing liquidity after Goswami Infratech debt had been extended twice. Delays in monetizing the group's 18.4% Tata Sons stake continued to complicate deleveraging.

After the New York close, Central Falls Detention Facility Corp. filed for Chapter 11. Occupancy and payments of roughly $180 per day for each federal detainee could not support more than $167 million of bond debt. The Rhode Island operator sought to eliminate over $100 million of obligations. The filing added a municipal project-credit case for the next session, exposing the dependence of tax-exempt debt on utilization and a concentrated government contract.

## Japan's Pension Signal Sends Yields Lower Before Any Mandate Changes

Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama urged pension funds, including GPIF, to invest more in Japanese financial assets. Twenty-year JGB yields fell 12 basis points to 3.745% and 10 years declined 11.5 to 2.76%; the yen gained as much as 0.7%. The possibility of a larger domestic buyer base was enough to reverse part of the week's pressure.

GPIF manages ¥293.6 trillion and holds about half overseas, while Japan owns roughly $1.2 trillion of Treasuries. A sustained move into domestic assets could support JGBs and reduce structural yen selling, but also leave less capital for foreign bonds. The immediate Japanese rally and the longer-run question for Treasury demand therefore pointed in different directions.

No mandate had changed. GPIF is overseen by the labor ministry and follows a five-year allocation process. Its March 2025 review retained equal 25% weights in domestic bonds, domestic equities, foreign bonds and foreign equities. Katayama's remarks shifted expectations well before any portfolio implementation.

Producer prices preserved the case for BOJ normalization. The corporate-goods index rose 7.1% in June from a year earlier, its fastest pace since early 2023, and 0.4% from May after an upward revision to the prior month. Wage settlements had exceeded 5% for a third year. A stronger pension bid could steady bonds without removing pressure from corporate prices and pay.

German final CPI was more mixed. June inflation slowed to 2.3% from May's 2.6%, with a 0.3% monthly decline. HICP rose 2.4% annually and fell 0.2% monthly. Energy dropped 3.0% on the month, led by motor fuel and heating oil, but core inflation held at 2.5% and services rose 3.1%. Cheaper energy softened the headline without settling the ECB's underlying inflation problem.

Canada added 18,000 jobs after May's 88,000 gain. The employment rate rose to 60.8%, unemployment eased to 6.5% and hourly wage growth accelerated to 3.3% from 3.0%. Manufacturing lost 17,000 jobs. The report was not uniformly strong, but firmer wages and lower unemployment limited the argument for near-term policy relief.

ECB member Emmanuel Moulin described AI as a possible near-term inflation force through capital spending and a later disinflationary force through productivity. It had not yet changed current policy. His distinction echoed the Fed's difficulty in assessing investment that supports activity now while promising efficiency gains later.

## Brazil's Inflation Surprise Contrasts With Senegal's Financing Squeeze

Brazilian annual inflation slowed to 4.64% in June, below every estimate in a survey with a 4.80% median. The monthly increase eased to 0.16%, the lowest since October, as food and beverages fell 0.24% against a 0.63% rise in housing. Following weak May job creation, the surprise strengthened the case for another quarter-point cut on August 5 after three consecutive reductions.

The Selic rate was still 14.25%, and central-bank projections placed end-2026 inflation above the target band's upper limit. Household debt-renegotiation support, subsidized credit and temporary suspension of some fuel taxes added stimulus ahead of the election. Softer current inflation gave room for gradual easing, but the fiscal backdrop constrained how far local yields could fall.

In Senegal, additional detail illustrated the scale of the debt problem already facing investors. An audit found about $7 billion of previously unreported loans; subsequent reviews lifted estimated public debt above 130% of GDP from an earlier 74%. The IMF suspended a $1.8 billion program, ratings fell deeper into junk and the sovereign lost effective Eurobond access. Average international-bond spreads exceeded 15 percentage points over Treasuries.

This year's debt repayments were about CFA5.5 trillion against expected tax revenue of roughly CFA5.4 trillion. Reliance on West African regional markets increased bank exposure to short government bills. Projects financed in euros and dollars depended on local-currency revenue, leaving the availability and timing of repayment funds critical alongside the debt stock. Restoring credible accounts and official financing mattered more than a favorable day in global markets.

Absa supplied a different regional risk through bank earnings. Net interest income generated 64% of group revenue, making large rate cuts in Kenya and Ghana important to profitability. Core regulatory capital was only modestly above the board's 11%–12.5% target range. Analysts questioned both acquisition capacity and a path to 16% return on equity. Downgrades helped leave the shares about 10% lower for the year while South African banks broadly gained around 7%. This was reduced room for expansion and weaker revenue, not an immediate capital breach.

EMB rose 0.03% to $95.99 despite higher Treasury yields. DXY edged up just 0.03% to 100.97, sparing borrowers a significant additional currency headwind. Index stability encompassed very different conditions: Brazilian inflation relief, Senegalese debt stress and Absa's exposure to lower regional rates.

## Equities Rise With Yields as Oil and Gold Decline

The S&P 500 gained 0.42% to 7,575.39, Nasdaq 100 rose 0.33% to 29,825.11 and semiconductors added 0.06% to 12,967.16. VIX fell 5.11% to 15.03. Investors accepted higher Treasury yields without a broad retreat from growth-sensitive assets.

WTI fell 0.93% to $71.41 and Brent declined 0.38% to $76.01. They remained 3.96% and 5.86% higher over the week, respectively, despite large monthly declines. Lower crude reduced the direct inflation impulse, while elevated refining margins and geopolitical disruption kept fuel costs uncertain.

Gold fell 0.64% to $4,104.10 as real yields rose. The dollar was almost unchanged at 100.97, so currency strength added little to the pressure on bullion. Gold's decline accompanied the higher real-rate hurdle rather than a broad flight into cash.

Calm currencies and wide rate differentials had helped G10 carry strategies return about 8% this year. Hedging costs were beginning to rise around the next US inflation release, however. With less Fed guidance, a large data surprise could unsettle leveraged carry positions and transmit through currencies, EM funding and cross-border bond demand, even after a quiet close.

## CPI, Warsh Testimony and Japan's Allocation Process Take Focus

June CPI and real earnings are due July 14 at 08:30 ET, followed by Kevin Warsh's House testimony at 10:00. PPI arrives July 15 at 08:30, before his Senate appearance at 10:00. Core and services prices will test whether lower energy is broadening into durable disinflation; real earnings will show the effect on purchasing power. Warsh's interpretation will matter after Friday's emphasis on both growth resilience and price stability.

Treasury offers $92 billion of 13-week and $79 billion of 26-week bills July 13 at 11:30 ET, then $95 billion of 42-day bills July 14 at the same time. All settle July 16. Bidding and secondary trading will indicate how comfortably money-market cash absorbs the supply after outer bill yields rose more than the shortest tenors.

Japan has no fixed date for a formal response from GPIF or the labor ministry. An allocation review, revised target bands or guidance to other public pensions would be a substantive development. Without those steps, the durability of Friday's JGB and yen rally remains uncertain. Any actual shift would also need to be assessed against the size of Japanese overseas holdings, rather than assuming domestic bond support is equally favorable for Treasuries.
